phase: research prototype; no product release or authorization claim
inputs: Exact owner-policy bytes bind exact evidence bytes, payer, token contract, finite horizon, per-intent caps/recipient/minimum non-refunded-and-not-burned settlement, and explicit transaction/receipt bindings.
assumptions: Unsigned reconstructed or owner-declared policy is trusted, not cryptographically authenticated.
Captured FINAL outcomes/action bodies and the declared token's SDK-compatible event/method semantics are trusted; no signature, state proof or source-to-WASM equivalence is verified.
A finite closed horizon is an owner declaration, not proof that no outside transaction exists.

separateQuantities.committedGross: Final successful payer-to-recipient transfer events, before refunds; failed receipts and self transfers contribute zero.
separateQuantities.returnedToPayer: Reverse transfer events in the causally linked resolver, not arbitrary same-amount incoming payments.
separateQuantities.burnedRefund: Canonical owner_id burn events for the receiver in that resolver; not delivery and not a payer refund.
separateQuantities.payerCost: Initial transfer minus causal returned tokens; includes any burned refund.
separateQuantities.settledAllocation: Initial transfer minus causal refund minus causal refund burn. It may have been spent/forwarded by the receiver and does not prove retained balance or useful work.
separateQuantities.resolverReportedUsed: Decoded resolver return; SDK can report the full amount when a refund is burned. It must not replace settledAllocation.
separateQuantities.usefulWork: Not assessed by this token-settlement profile; native utility evaluation remains separate.
separateQuantities.rights: Ledger/right conservation remains a separate owner reference; no generic rights verdict is inferred from token flows alone.

correlation: Match receipt body ID to its outcome executor and its creation predecessor; enforce root signer propagation except native system refunds.
Plain ft_transfer supports atomic batches of plain transfer actions assigned to one intent; event tuples and action tuples must agree. Split receipts and independent equal-price intents remain valid.
Single-action ft_transfer_call requires its returned resolver receipt, matching sender/receiver/amount, hook arguments/msg and the exact hook output-data ID consumed by the resolver.
Same tuple/amount, a memo saying refund, graph creation siblings or root SuccessValue alone are insufficient callback correlation.

Resolver U must agree with amount minus the causal refund. Refund plus burn is bounded by the hook's SDK-compatible unused amount; failure/malformed/oversized hook output defaults to the original amount. Unknown receiver balance prevents a refund-sufficiency claim.
Missing/ambiguous callback/body/data-ID evidence keeps settlement unknown; known final gross over a cap still proves a breach.

Mixing multiple asynchronous calls within one receipt is initially unsupported for settlement attribution; observed gross bounds still remain available. This limit does not redefine the long-term scope.
observations: Group by transaction identity; duplicate identical observations are idempotent. Merge compatible FINAL node/body maps with source references. Conflicting FINAL identities remain explicit; no choosing a convenient observation or erasing known violations in other transactions.
decision: Separate per-intent committed-gross, recipient, burned-refund cap and settlement-minimum results. Overall breach/failure has priority over unrelated unknown evidence; otherwise any incomplete/conflicting/unsupported evidence prevents an overall within result. No payment is sent or signed.
referenceAuthorship: SDK source and type semantics have external authorship. Original literal numeric reference, synthetic envelopes, selection, extractor and policy checker are ours, source-informed; not blind or independent end-to-end grading.
publicationGate: Do not publish as a generic token policy engine before source binding, causal counterexamples, split/equal-price allowed controls, partial/conflicting evidence and Python/browser boundaries are verified.
Preserve the original observed records, source-informed reference, failures and post-result corrections; do not silently relabel constructed evidence as an execution.
